info.title: grassmoth study API
info.description:
Seven actions carry out a study. Set the question with `edit_question` and build
the model with `edit_model`. Upload tables with `/api/upload`, extract
observations with `prepare_data`, and condition the model on them with `fit`.
`simulate` samples an authored or fitted model; `data_diff` and `model_diff`
compare saved revisions. `/api/docs` has complete input/output schemas, defaults
and alternatives.

- **Submit and poll:** POST JSON `{action, input, reasoning}` to
  `/api/studies/{workspace_id}/{action}`; `reasoning` is optional. Poll GET
  `/api/studies/{workspace_id}/{action}/{call_id}` until `status` is `success` or
  `failed`. GET never starts or retries work; an unknown call returns 404.
- **Results and errors:** `body` contains the action's scientific output only on
  success; otherwise it is null. `messages` holds progress, traces and failure
  details. Completed results are saved and GET never recomputes them.
- **JSON responses:** send `Accept: application/json` on action POST/GET to read
  results with curl and jq. Numerical values are nested lists; non-finite values
  are null. Workspace, timeline, upload and HTTP error responses are also JSON.
- **Call reuse:** revision selectors accept exact Git hashes or `"latest"`, pinned
  once at POST. Identical resolved inputs reuse running calls, successes **and
  failures**. Changing `reasoning` does not create a new call; change the inputs
  to make a new attempt.
- **Artifact references:** response `commit_id` identifies the call's journal entry.
  For subsequent inputs, GET `/api/studies/{workspace_id}/timeline`, find the call,
  and select the required artifact by `artifact_id` in
  `record.attempt.outcome.effects.produced`. Use its `revision` for model,
  question, data and fit references.
- **Read-only access:** `/api/workspaces` reports `X-Actions-Enabled`. With
  `READ_ONLY_FACADE=1`, saved calls remain readable; an unsaved POST returns 403.

get.description: Read an existing call by ID. Never resolve inputs, start a workflow, execute, or retry. The envelope and accumulated messages match POST, including cached failures.

post.description: Set the study question from input.question. POST returns a call_id; GET polls it. Identical resolved calls reuse both successes and failures.

Merge input.dynamical_model_spec into input.parent_ref: start empty for a question revision, or retain omitted fields from a model revision and its pinned question. Null entity entries delete their IDs. Prune constructs outside the outcome ancestry with warnings, then validate and evaluate data-independent model checks. The body contains the produced model and its findings; messages retain all execution logging. GET polls the returned call_id.

Prepare observations from uploaded tables using the selected model's definitions. input.source is a folder under data/{workspace_id}/, including subfolders. CSV and Parquet tables must supply a date or datetime timestamp column and are concatenated in captured file order. Source bytes and revision selectors are pinned before computing call identity. GET polls call_id.

Fit target.new model and data, or continue target.fit_ref at its last retained state. Counts request additional draws; zero warmup freezes tuning and algorithm changes require warmup. Zero warmup and zero samples compile both sweep programs without execution. Zero-draw fits return checks and inference without a conditioned model. repeat distinguishes timing attempts. GET polls call_id.

Simulate input.dynamical_model_spec_ref using input.simulation. The model owns deterministic inputs and retained trajectory coordinates; authored initial states apply at simulation.start. body.data contains an array of observation histories of the same type returned by prepare_data. The successful body requires data and report; report owns single or paired numerical evidence, calculated summaries and causal findings; messages retain traces. GET polls call_id.

Compare input.left_ref and input.right_ref, each a nonempty list of {revision, replicate_index} references. Omit the index to compare all recorded histories. Data latest selects prepared user data; simulations require exact Git hashes. Retain the complete comparison in Git. GET polls call_id. Identical resolved calls reuse successes and failures; the comparison is the body.

Compare input.before_ref and input.after_ref as saved DynamicalModelSpec documents. Return changes using the same partial DynamicalModelSpec contract as edit_model: omissions are unchanged and null map entries delete identities. Retain the patch in Git. GET polls call_id. Identical resolved calls reuse successes and failures; the comparison is the body.

get.description: Slim call log: call IDs, retained arguments, outcome summaries and dependencies. The viewer reads complete results and messages with GET using each call_id.

Available workspaces and their immutable study questions.

X-Actions-Enabled reports whether the facade accepts new calls.

AdaptedLatentStepSpec-Input.description: Warmup adapts the per-time scale towards the assigned movement target.

target.description: Fraction of proposals at each time step that should change its state. In a new fit every time step's scale starts at 0.01, adapts towards this target during warmup and is then frozen. Corenflos & Särkkä (2025, section 4) target 0.5 per time step, below Finke & Thiery's 1 - (N + 1)^(-1/3), because a higher target can be unreachable at some time steps and leaves the sampler stuck there. Corenflos & Finke (2024, section 5.2) use 0.75 and note that the optimum depends on N and on the state dimension.

DataComparisonReport.description:
Statistical comparison of two nonempty selections of immutable saved histories.

Compare data preparation revisions, observations with prior or posterior
simulations, or simulations across model specifications, priors, fits and
intervention scenarios.

Left/right name comparison sides, not temporal revisions or an editing language.
Resolved references retain every selected replicate in request order; a history
cannot occur twice within one side. Variables are ordered by indicator identity.
Exogenous indicators supplied by a simulation's model are excluded.

One-versus-one comparisons expose point changes. One-versus-many comparisons
evaluate predictive checks against the singleton reference. Many-versus-many
comparisons retain per-history statistics without pairing draws or evaluating
reference-based checks. IndicatorComparison owns the exact change semantics.
Source definitions and complete observations belong to prepare_data/simulate
results; this report owns only selection identity and newly computed evidence.
DataComparisonReport.title: DataComparisonReport

method.description: Auxiliary law for conditional dSMC. particle_rwm (kappa 0) centres the auxiliary point on the current state. particle_amala (Algorithm 3) drifts it along the gradient of the local prior and observation terms; particle_amala_plus (Algorithm 5) adds the next transition. With gradients the scale need only shrink like D^(-1/3) as the state dimension D grows, against D^(-1) without (Corenflos & Finke 2024, figure 1). There aMALA+ had up to three times Particle-RWM's ESS and twice aMALA's, for twice aMALA's gradients (section 5.4). On a GPU, Corenflos & Särkkä (2025) found gradient and plain proposals equally efficient per second (section 4.1), with gradients more robust to sticky dynamics and very informative observations (section 4.4).

num_particles.description: Particles per sweep, including the current path. More particles give each time step more candidates, but each dSMC merge scores N x N candidate pairs, so memory and work per merge grow as N^2 (Corenflos, Chopin & Särkkä 2022, section 4).

latent_step.description: Per-time-step scale: adapted towards a movement target, or fixed.

latent_block_coords.description: State coordinates proposed per sweep, drawn uniformly from the free ones; the others keep their current paths at every time step. 1 proposes one coordinate's whole path, all proposes the full state. Importance weights degenerate as the proposed dimension grows, which blocking counters (Corenflos & Särkkä 2025, section 3.1): smaller blocks keep larger scales at the same movement rate, but each coordinate is proposed only every D/k sweeps, and coupled coordinates move slowly when proposed apart.

pilot_mixture.description: Mix two fixed Gaussians into every candidate draw: 85% of candidates come from the local auxiliary proposal, 10% from a Gaussian at the initializer's mean path with a quarter of its variance, and 5% from one with four times its variance. GaussianReferenceTemperingSpec-Input.description:
Replica exchange; each ladder retains only its exact beta-one chain.

The ladder spans beta one to zero. The reference is fixed at initialization,
its endpoint is independently refreshed every sweep, and even/odd neighboring
swaps alternate. Rejection-based ladder adaptation runs during the first half
of warmup, leaving the rest to settle before retaining posterior draws.

It is for posteriors whose chains stay in separate modes: states that move freely
under the reference reach the exact chain through swaps (Syed et al. 2022). Its
limits are in docs/assumptions.md, under Model class.

num_temperatures.description: Replicas per chain, initially evenly spaced from beta one (the exact posterior) to beta zero (the Gaussian reference). Each replica runs a full sweep, so cost grows linearly. With alternating even/odd swaps the round-trip rate tends to 1 / (2 + 2Λ) instead of collapsing as replicas are added, and about 2Λ replicas are optimal, where Λ is the posterior's communication barrier (Syed et al. 2022, sections 4.2 and 5.3).

reference_scale.description: Multiplies the reference's standard deviations for parameters and path innovations. The reference is built at initialization from the starting draws and the transition Jacobians along their mean path. Above 1 it covers mass the starting draws missed, but overlaps the posterior less, which raises the barrier and so the replicas needed.

adaptation_interval.description: Sweeps between ladder updates in the first half of warmup. Each update respaces the temperatures to equalize the swap rejection rates estimated since the last update (Syed et al. 2022, sections 5.1-5.2). An interval above half the warmup leaves the evenly spaced ladder unadapted.

GuidedPathSpec-Input.description:
Sequential conditional SMC with exact Gaussian transition-informed proposals.

Corenflos & Finke (2024). Parameter labels remain marginalized, and exact nonlinear
transitions and densities pay every weight, so each method's approximation costs
mixing, never the target.

method.description: particle_agrad keeps the auxiliary variable in the weights (section 4.1); strong future information or multiple modes can reduce its mixing. twisted_particle_agrad adds a Gaussian look-ahead built at the auxiliary path: a parallel backward information scan guides the sequential filter, and proposals combine exact nonlinear transition means with the approximate twist, whose normalized densities and twist ratios are paid in full (section 4.4); poor local fits and multiple modes cost efficiency. particle_mgrad integrates the path auxiliary out of the particle weights with the untwisted proposal (section 4.2); it supports point readings without deterministic recurrences, and separated path components and informative future readings can slow its mixing.
method.title: Method

num_particles.description: Particles per sweep, including the current path. Each extends a parent chosen at the previous time, so work grows linearly in particles and times, and the filter's depth grows linearly with the number of times (Corenflos & Finke 2024, section 4.7).
num_particles.title: Num Particles

latent_step.description: Per-time-step scale: adapted towards a movement target, or fixed. Small scales keep proposals near the current path; large ones let the dynamics dominate, approaching conditional SMC with the transition as proposal (Corenflos & Finke 2024, section 4.6).

kappa.description: 1 shifts the auxiliary point along the gradient of the observation densities, mixed over parameter labels; 0 omits it (Corenflos & Finke 2024, Algorithm 6). The shift is a Langevin step on the observation term: for a Gaussian reading it overshoots once the scale exceeds four times that reading's variance.
kappa.title: Kappa

scan_unroll.description: Time steps per iteration of the forward filter and backward-selection loops. Unrolling changes how XLA compiles these sequential loops, not the algorithm or its target. Each step runs small kernels, so on a GPU per-iteration overhead is a large share of a sweep; unrolling amortizes it at the cost of a larger program and longer compilation. A CPU has little such overhead to remove. 1 disables unrolling.
scan_unroll.title: Scan Unroll

prefix_mixture.description: Opt in to per-parameter-label local Gaussian proposals, mixed with the unfloored prefix label probabilities. Every particle pays the full mixture density; the shared auxiliary law and look-ahead remain unchanged. Requires twisted_particle_agrad with kappa=1 and point readings without replay. Early label collapse, poor shared guidance and separated modes can reduce mixing.
prefix_mixture.title: Prefix Mixture

num_particles.description: Particles per sweep, including the current path. Each extends a parent chosen at the previous time, so work grows linearly in particles and times, and the filter's depth grows linearly with the number of times (Corenflos & Finke 2024, section 4.7).
num_particles.title: Num Particles

latent_step.description: Per-time-step scale: adapted towards a movement target, or fixed. Small scales keep proposals near the current path; large ones let the dynamics dominate, approaching conditional SMC with the transition as proposal (Corenflos & Finke 2024, section 4.6).

kappa.description: 1 shifts the auxiliary point along the gradient of the observation densities, mixed over parameter labels; 0 omits it (Corenflos & Finke 2024, Algorithm 6). The shift is a Langevin step on the observation term: for a Gaussian reading it overshoots once the scale exceeds four times that reading's variance.
kappa.title: Kappa

scan_unroll.description: Time steps per iteration of the forward filter and backward-selection loops. Unrolling changes how XLA compiles these sequential loops, not the algorithm or its target. Each step runs small kernels, so on a GPU per-iteration overhead is a large share of a sweep; unrolling amortizes it at the cost of a larger program and longer compilation. A CPU has little such overhead to remove. 1 disables unrolling.
scan_unroll.title: Scan Unroll

prefix_mixture.description: Opt in to per-parameter-label local Gaussian proposals, mixed with the unfloored prefix label probabilities. Every particle pays the full mixture density; the shared auxiliary law and look-ahead remain unchanged. Requires twisted_particle_agrad with kappa=1 and point readings without replay. Early label collapse, poor shared guidance and separated modes can reduce mixing.

MarginalParticleGibbsSpec-Input.description:
Marginalized parameter ensemble and exact conditional trajectory updates.

m-PGibbs (Corenflos 2025), the default sampler, proposes parameter particles around
a shared auxiliary point, runs conditional SMC against the posterior mixture over
them and selects a parameter together with the new path. Parameter moves are thus
marginalized over paths, as in PMMH, instead of conditioned on one. The proposal
covariance starts from the initializer and is re-estimated at the end of each
warmup window (section 3.4).

n_parameter_particles.description: Parameter particles M per sweep: the current value and M - 1 proposals around one auxiliary point. Work grows as O(TNM); Corenflos (2025, section 5) recommends M = 2, given the weak performance of larger ensembles (Pozza & Zanella 2024).
n_parameter_particles.title: N Parameter Particles

tempering.description: untempered runs the exact posterior alone; gaussian_reference runs Gaussian-reference parallel tempering.

compiler_reparameterization.description: Compute time-indexed path translations from Gauss-Newton mean cross curvature, including deterministic recurrences and interval readings. Build at mean initial parameters and their IEKS path; rebuild at cold-chain mean parameters and their IEKS path at warmup window ends. Freeze before retained draws and preserve the chart in native continuation state. Every density and reported path retains the exact physical model. Local slopes, strong nonlinearity and multiple modes can limit mixing.
compiler_reparameterization.title: Compiler Reparameterization

scale_chart.description: Rescale each stochastic state's deviations from a center path by the change in its own diffusion scale, in the sampler's actual parameter coordinates: structural non-centring of the diffusion. The center is the mean warmup path in the translated chart, learned in the existing warmup windows and frozen before retained draws. Every label pays the exact log-Jacobian, and all densities and reported paths retain the exact physical model. Requires a guided path update and point readings without deterministic recurrences. Data-pinned deviations, a poor center or a state-dependent diffusion cost efficiency, never the target.
scale_chart.title: Scale Chart

parameter_proposal.description: random_walk splits a preconditioned Gaussian step into two symmetric halves through the auxiliary point. pseudo_langevin drifts the first half along the log-posterior gradient at a path fixed when the kernel is built, and corrects the asymmetry exactly in the selection weights; the current path would break that correction (Corenflos 2025, section 3.1). It is kept as the control for gradients within the same kernel.

diagnostic_metrics.description: Optional traces to record: particle_identity (the selected particle per time step, reference-path hit rate and distinct selected particles), parameter_movement (RMS parameter jump) and particle_weights (dSMC weight ESS, entropy and spread per tree node). frequency_refresh summarizes retained path movement in DCT bands; regional_movement summarizes movement and frozen step sizes over existing question windows and reading coverage, with the ten worst times. They cost memory and output size, and no convergence check reads them; they explain a failing sampler.

param_target_accept.description: Target fraction of sweeps in which the parameters move to a proposed particle. Selection is a Barker-type step (Corenflos 2025, section 3.3), whose optimal rate for random-walk proposals is about 0.27 in one dimension and 0.158 in high dimension (Agrawal et al. 2023).
param_target_accept.title: Param Target Accept

adaptation_scheme.description: How warmup adapts the parameter step: simple uses a constant gain and keeps the last step; dual_averaging keeps the averaged step at the end of warmup (Hoffman & Gelman 2014, section 3.2).

initialization.description: Independent Gaussian starts, which also set the initial proposal scale.

NutsDASpec-Input.description:
Joint HMC with dual averaging and windowed diagonal mass adaptation.

It moves every parameter and free latent coordinate at once on the exact joint
density, with no particle approximation. It also reconstructs deterministic
recurrences that the particle samplers reject, and is a diagnostic when particle
chains fail to converge.

parameterization.description: Coordinates the sampler moves in; the posterior is the same in all three, only its geometry changes. centred samples each path directly, standardized by the prior's per-step covariances at the starting parameters. non_centred samples each free coordinate's Euler-Maruyama innovation and rebuilds the path from the current parameters. mixed keeps coordinates with a direct point reading centred and makes the rest non-centred. Centred mixes well where data pin the states, non-centred where data are weak against the dynamics (Papaspiliopoulos, Roberts & Sköld 2007). Frozen per fit; changing it on a continued fit requires warmup.

target_accept_prob.description: Mean acceptance statistic that dual averaging steers the step size towards during warmup (Hoffman & Gelman 2014, section 3.2). Raising it towards 0.9-0.99 shrinks the step, which removes divergences in strongly curved regions at the cost of longer trajectories. 0.8 is the NumPyro and Stan default.
target_accept_prob.title: Target Accept Prob
